deep.reconstruction:
Setting: for lambda=(lambda_i) in l^1 and n>=0, let alpha_n(lambda)=e_n(lambda) be the n-th elementary symmetric function in infinitely many variables. These are the Taylor coefficients of the genus-zero canonical product f_lambda(z)=prod(1+lambda_i z) = sum alpha_n(lambda) z^n. Up to a constant factor (and the factor z^k), these are exactly the coefficients of an arbitrary entire function of genus zero.

Trivial bound: |alpha_n(lambda)| <= ||lambda||_1^n / n!. Hence each n! alpha_n is an n-homogeneous polynomial of norm <= 1 on l^1. The norm is in fact exactly 1, as the vectors (1/N,...,1/N) show (n! C(N,n)/N^n -> 1).

Proposition. For every lambda in l^1 the series S(lambda)=sum n! alpha_n(lambda) converges absolutely. The power series of S at 0 has radius 1 (uniform convergence on balls of radius < 1). S is holomorphic on finite-dimensional subspaces; indeed S(z lambda)=sum n! alpha_n(lambda) z^n is entire in z. Grothendieck adds that S is not bounded on the unit ball and claims it is 'not an entire function' of lambda.

Corollary. The proposition is equivalent to (n! |alpha_n|)^{1/n} -> 0, i.e. |alpha_n|^{1/n}=o(1/n), i.e. alpha_n = eps_n^n/n! with eps_n -> 0 (by Stirling). Equivalently, every genus-zero entire function sum a_n z^n satisfies these relations. In modern terms: a genus-zero product with sum |1/z_k| < infinity has order <= 1 and exponential type 0.

Proof (next page). Reduce to lambda_i > 0 decreasing. Use Cauchy's inequality alpha_n <= M(R)/R^n with M(R)=prod(1+lambda_i R). Split the product at n+1, bound the tail by exp(rho_{n+1} R), and choose R=(n+1)/rho_{n+1}. This gives alpha_n <= e^n prod_{k<=n+1}(rho_k/k + lambda_k), and lambda_k = o(1/k) yields alpha_n <= e^n eps_1...eps_{n+1}/(n+1)!.

Context. The previous page (Jensen-type formulas bounding zero counts by M(r)) and this page are preparatory estimates on entire functions of genus 0 / order <= 1. These are exactly the estimates needed for Fredholm determinants det(1+zT)=prod(1+lambda_i z) of nuclear/trace-class operators with summable eigenvalues. This points to Grothendieck's 'La theorie de Fredholm' (1956) and the Produits tensoriels topologiques material.

Modern reading. S(lambda)=integral_0^infinity e^{-t} prod(1+lambda_i t) dt is the Laplace/Borel transform of the canonical product, evaluated at 1. In infinite-dimensional holomorphy, S is an example of a function holomorphic on all of l^1 but not of bounded type: its radius of boundedness and the radius of uniform convergence of its Taylor series at 0 both equal 1.
errors: The claim that S 'n'est pas une fonction entiere' of lambda is false in the modern sense. S is Gateaux-holomorphic everywhere. It is also locally bounded: |S(lambda0+mu)| <= integral e^{-(1-||mu||)t} prod(1+|lambda0_i| t) dt, which is finite uniformly for ||mu|| <= r < 1, because the product has exponential type 0. So S is Frechet-holomorphic on all of l^1, an entire function not of bounded type. Grothendieck's statement is only correct if 'entiere' means 'Taylor series at 0 converges uniformly on bounded sets / bounded on bounded sets'. The page does not distinguish the two notions.
The bound alpha_n(lambda) <= ||lambda||_1^n/n! should be stated for |alpha_n(lambda)| when lambda is complex. This is minor.
In the Cauchy estimate on the next page, the exponent should be R^n, not R^{n+1}. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Coefficients of genus-zero entire functions viewed as elementary symmetric functions of an l^1 sequence; the estimate (n!|a_n|)^{1/n} -> 0 (exponential type zero)
ideas.modern_name: Lindelof's theorem on type of canonical products / coefficient characterization of exponential type 0
ideas.where_published: Possibly used in 'La theorie de Fredholm' (Bull. SMF 1956) for Fredholm determinants of nuclear operators

ideas.what: S(lambda)=sum n! e_n(lambda) on l^1: absolutely convergent everywhere, Taylor radius 1 at 0, unbounded on the unit ball
ideas.modern_name: Entire (holomorphic) function on a Banach space not of bounded type; radius of boundedness smaller than the radius of Gateaux holomorphy
ideas.usually_credited_to: Infinite-dimensional holomorphy: Nachbin (1960s), Dineen; the classical counterexample is sum z_n^n on c_0

ideas.what: Cauchy-estimate proof with an optimized split radius R=(n+1)/rho_{n+1}

missed.claim: This is a very early (1953) explicit example of a function on a Banach space (l^1) that is holomorphic everywhere but not of bounded type, given by a natural symmetric-function construction. Its Taylor series at 0 has radius 1. Nachbin-style examples of this phenomenon are usually dated to the 1960s. Grothendieck himself mislabels it as 'not entire'.
missed.quote: La fonction lambda -> S(lambda) est holomorphe au voisinage de 0, avec un rayon de convergence egal a 1 ... Cependant, cette fonction n'est pas bornee dans la boule unite de l^1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority detail for infinite-dimensional holomorphy (holomorphy types, bounded type vs entire). It is a natural example linking Fredholm determinants / symmetric functions of trace-class spectra to the Borel transform. It is not a new theorem.

missed.claim: Implicitly links the Borel/Laplace transform of Fredholm determinants (S = integral e^{-t} det(1+tT) dt over the eigenvalue sequence) with holomorphy on the space of summable spectra.
missed.quote: on obtient, a un facteur pres, les coefficients les plus generaux d'une fonction entiere de genre zero
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; the analytic content is classical. The angle of treating spectra as points of l^1 and the determinant map as a holomorphic map is natural in later Fredholm-determinant literature (Simon).

deep.surprise_reason: The analytic core (genus-zero products have exponential type 0) is classical. The mildly interesting point is an early, natural example of an everywhere-holomorphic but unbounded-on-balls function on l^1, which Grothendieck does not correctly identify as entire. The page is preparatory to his published Fredholm theory.
transcription_corrections: Title reads 'Sur une certaine fonction holomorphe [continue struck] sur l'espace de Banach l^1'.

Final lines of the corollary likely read: 'Si sum a_n z^n est une fonction entiere de genre zero, les [deux relations] des a_n [...] sont verifiees'. The next page refers to 'Les deux relations indiquees ci-dessus'.
'On a' after the definition of alpha_n is likely right ('On a. alpha_n(lambda) <= ||lambda||_1^n/n!').
